nodes.description: aggregate(Call[] memory calls) public: loops over caller-supplied Call structs and performs a low-level call on each target with the supplied callData, returning block.number and an array of return data.
getEthBalance(address addr) public view: returns the ETH balance of the given address.
getBlockHash(uint256 blockNumber) public view: returns blockhash(blockNumber) for the caller-supplied block number.
getCurrentBlockTimestamp() public view: returns block.timestamp, exposing miner-influenced time to callers.
getCurrentBlockCoinbase() public view: returns block.coinbase, the block miner address.
block.timestamp: miner-manipulable environment value read inside getCurrentBlockTimestamp.
calls[i].target.call(calls[i].callData): arbitrary external low-level call to an attacker-chosen address with attacker-chosen data, executed inside the aggregate loop.
calls: caller-supplied array of Call structs (target address plus callData) that fully determines which external calls aggregate performs.
addr: caller-supplied address whose balance is read by getEthBalance.
blockNumber: caller-supplied block number passed to blockhash in getBlockHash.
i: loop counter in aggregate that drives iteration over the calls array and thus drives the external call execution.
success: boolean returned by the low-level call in aggregate, used to decide whether the returned bytes are recorded.
ret: raw bytes returned by the low-level call in aggregate.
returnData: dynamically sized bytes array allocated as new bytes[](calls.length) and filled inside the aggregate loop.

edges.reason: The caller-controlled calls array supplies both the target address and the calldata consumed by the low-level external call, so untrusted input flows directly into the unsafe operation.
The low-level external call in aggregate transfers control to an arbitrary attacker-supplied contract, which can re-enter aggregate or other functions before the loop finishes writing returnData.
aggregate's loop body is the control-flow location where the low-level call on calls[i].target is executed.
The loop index i governs how many times and on which Call struct the unsafe external call is invoked.
The success flag returned by the external call gates whether ret is stored into the returnData array.
The raw bytes ret returned by the external call are copied into the returnData result array.
block.timestamp is read and returned by getCurrentBlockTimestamp, making the function's output depend on a miner-manipulable environment value.
The addr parameter is used to read the ETH balance returned by getEthBalance.
The blockNumber parameter is passed to the blockhash builtin in getBlockHash and drives the returned hash.

normalization_plan.reason: The calls parameter is the direct source of the target and calldata used by the unsafe low-level call in aggregate, so it should be normalized into that unsafe_operation node.
The addr parameter is only used inside getEthBalance to read that address's balance, so it can be merged into the getEthBalance function node.
The blockNumber parameter exists solely as the argument to blockhash inside getBlockHash, so it can be merged into the getBlockHash function node.

The loop counter i is a purely local iteration variable that only determines which attacker-supplied Call is passed to the unsafe low-level call, so it should be normalized into that unsafe_operation node.
The success flag is local bookkeeping of the low-level call's result and has no meaning outside that call site, so it should be normalized into the unsafe_operation node.
The ret local holds the bytes returned by the low-level call and is tied directly to that call site, so it should be normalized into the unsafe_operation node.
The returnData local is the aggregate function's own result buffer populated inside its loop, so it should be normalized into the aggregate function node.
